scope_notes: Profile skill-pack: the product is one 66-line SKILL.md that shapes agent behaviour, plus a benchmark that backs its claims against REA. Flags changed from the suggestion: parses_untrusted true (the targets are third-party binaries, app bundles, firmware and websites, SKILL.md:3), distributed true (installed and updated via 'npx skills add/update', README.md:51-61). executes_code true because the skill drives the agent's shell. SEC-4 NA (the artefact bundles no third-party components), SEC-5 NA (no CI), MNT-1 NA (no code architecture). The product is judged by the agent behaviour it asks for, its claims and its benchmark.

red_line_decisions.SEC-6: Not triggered (level 2): no secrets committed; missing redaction guidance is a gap.
red_line_decisions.SEC-7: Not triggered (level 2): no untrusted input reaches a shell string or eval in shipped code; running targets without isolation is scored as a gap.
red_line_decisions.EPI-5: Not triggered (level 2): the headline overgeneralises but no number is contradicted by the committed data, which reproduces exactly.

gaps.title: No rule for untrusted content read from targets
gaps.case: The skill sends agents to read strings, bundle slices, web pages and captures of third-party software (leanrea/SKILL.md:23,31,52,54) and has no rule that this content is data, not instructions; bench/tasks.json has no injection case.
gaps.impact: Text planted in an analysed target can steer an agent that holds a shell (OWASP LLM01).
gaps.fix: Add a rule that target content is untrusted data and never a source of commands; add a benchmark target with planted instructions.

gaps.title: Headline equivalence exceeds the benchmark
gaps.case: README.md:3 says the file 'does what REA does' and README.md:24 'at the same accuracy', from 4 tasks on 3 targets, one model, 3 reps (74/75 vs 75/75). A paired bootstrap of bench/results/final.jsonl gives leanrea/REA wall ratio 0.63 [0.51, 0.76] (robust, 12/12 cells) but leanrea/no-skill wall ratio 0.87 [0.70, 1.05], so 'about 19% faster' (README.md:46) is not separable from no change.
gaps.impact: Agents and people choosing a tool from the README get a broader claim than the measurement supports.
gaps.fix: Scope the headline to the measured tasks, report intervals, and rerun with at least 5 interleaved reps.

gaps.title: Committed results are not the shipped harness's output and cannot be audited
gaps.case: bench/run_all.sh:5-7 runs reps 1..REPS and appends to results/run.jsonl, but the committed bench/results/final.jsonl holds reps 11-13; answers are written only to the gitignored work directory (bench/run.py:50), so only miss lists such as ['event ch'] are visible.
gaps.impact: Grades and the stated reason for the one miss (README.md:24) cannot be checked, and whether other reps were run is not stated.
gaps.fix: Commit the full run log with answers (or their hashes) and document how final.jsonl was produced.

gaps.title: Lenient regex graders without self-tests
gaps.case: bench/tasks.json:43 ('hash': 'hash'), :45 ('sock': '\.sock') and :48 ('json': 'JSON') pass any answer that mentions the word; bench/run.py:44 applies them with no known-good or known-bad check; BENCHMARK.md:41 records a false negative fixed by hand.
gaps.impact: Score parity between arms can hide wrong answers.
gaps.fix: Give every key a known-good and a known-bad answer checked before scoring, and tighten the keys.

gaps.title: Unpinned registry packages executed on every use
gaps.case: leanrea/SKILL.md:29 and :38 run 'npx -y @electron/asar' and 'npx -y @electron/fuses', :39 'npx -y prettier', each fetching and running the latest version without confirmation.
gaps.impact: Supply-chain exposure on the analyst's machine at every run.
gaps.fix: Pin versions in the snippets or require the preinstalled tools listed in the Install section.

gaps.title: No isolation for parsing or running untrusted targets
gaps.case: Extractors and parsers (binwalk -e, unblob -e, jadx, apktool; leanrea/SKILL.md:47,53) and runtime rows that launch or attach to the target (frida -f, lldb -p, Electron --inspect; :55) run directly on the host with no sandbox, VM or consent step.
gaps.impact: A malicious target can exploit parser defects or run code with the analyst's privileges.
gaps.fix: Recommend a disposable VM or container for extraction and dynamic analysis, and require consent before launching a target.

gaps.title: macOS-only first moves presented as universal
gaps.case: 'cp -c' (APFS clone, leanrea/SKILL.md:11), lipo, otool, xcrun dyld_info and codesign (:23,41) and $TMPDIR (unset on many Linux hosts, so 'rm -rf $X' targets /re/asar, :29) are in the paste-and-run moves; the README states macOS only for the benchmark (README.md:16).
gaps.impact: On Linux the native first move fails and costs the turns the skill aims to save.
gaps.fix: State the platform scope, add a Linux first move (readelf, nm, objdump), default TMPDIR and quote variables.

gaps.title: No versions; benchmark keys tied to one app build
gaps.case: 'npx skills update leanrea' pulls the latest (README.md:61); there are no tags or changelog; answer keys match Notion 7.35.1 and go1.27.1 only (README.md:107, bench/setup.sh:18).
gaps.impact: Users cannot pin a known-good skill, and the benchmark stops being rerunnable as the targets update.
gaps.fix: Tag releases, record the skill commit in each result row, and keep keys per target version.

gaps.title: No authorised-use note for reverse engineering
gaps.case: Neither README.md nor leanrea/SKILL.md mentions licence terms or legal limits of reverse engineering, while the benchmark reverse engineers a proprietary app (bench/setup.sh:7-13).
gaps.impact: Users and agents get no guardrail on authorised use.
gaps.fix: Add a short note on authorised use and where interoperability exceptions apply.

opportunities.title: Cheap-probe front end for REA and rex
opportunities.description: On the same operations raw commands took 0.04-4.8 s where REA's CLI took 0.56-47.9 s (bench/BENCHMARK.md:67-73), and RE4exa's lens run answered 7 answer-key questions in 219 ms. Routing first questions through leanrea's router and keeping REA for typed relations, evidence records and graph queries combines the speed with REA's provenance.

opportunities.title: Adopt ponytail's benchmark hygiene
opportunities.description: ponytail's agentic harness interleaves arms, runs 5 reps, self-tests every grader with good and bad references before spending (DietrichGebert__ponytail benchmarks/agentic/run.py:205-229) and reports bootstrap intervals; leanrea's 3-rep side-by-side design (bench/run_all.sh:5-7) cannot separate leanrea from no skill (wall ratio 0.87 [0.70, 1.05]). One shared harness also gives a common answer-key format with RE4exa's REA answer key.

opportunities.title: Machine-readable router table
opportunities.description: The 19-row router (leanrea/SKILL.md:35-55) as data (detect pattern, command, fallback, output cap, platform), rendered into SKILL.md, would fix the macOS-only first moves, make each row testable on fixture binaries, and let rea, rex and pandacode reuse the same routing.

opportunities.title: Run the recipe inside agent-sandbox-lockdown
opportunities.description: agent-sandbox-lockdown provides a Docker sandbox with DNS and egress allowlists, least-privilege tools, approval for writes and a JSONL tool-call log (its README). Running leanrea's extraction and runtime rows there closes the isolation gap without changing the recipe's commands.

opportunities.title: Attention rules as host hooks
opportunities.description: 'Never cat a big file', 'cap every output' and '2-4 tool calls' are prose (leanrea/SKILL.md:14-18). A pre-tool hook of the kind ponytail ships for Claude Code and Codex (hooks/claude-codex-hooks.json there) could warn on uncapped output commands and count calls, making the budget enforceable.

reengineering.gain: Claims with uncertainty and auditable grading
reengineering.measure: Interleaved arms with at least 5 reps; paired bootstrap interval on leanrea/no-skill excludes 1 or the claim is withdrawn; every key rejects a known-wrong answer before scoring; answers committed

reengineering.gain: Platform-correct first moves and a reusable routing table
reengineering.measure: SKILL.md stays at or under 8 KB; Linux and macOS first moves both succeed on fixture ELF and Mach-O binaries

reengineering.gain: Agents resist planted instructions and do not run unpinned or untrusted code by default
reengineering.measure: A benchmark target with planted instructions is followed in 0 of 5 runs; rg finds no unpinned 'npx -y' in SKILL.md

questions.question: Do the README's benchmark totals follow from the committed raw data?
questions.answer: Yes: recomputed from bench/results/final.jsonl (leanrea 387.7 s, $2.17, 55 turns, 2.40 M tokens, 74/75; REA 627.4 s, $3.36, 124, 5.93 M, 75/75; percentages 38.2, 35.4, 55.6, 59.5).

questions.question: Is leanrea faster than REA and than no skill?
questions.answer: Faster and cheaper than REA in 12 of 12 paired cells (wall ratio 0.63, 95% bootstrap 0.51-0.76); against no skill the wall-time difference is not distinguishable from zero at n=3 (0.87, 0.70-1.05) and cost is equal.

questions.question: Is the skill safe to point at untrusted software?
questions.answer: Not as written: it has no untrusted-content rule, no isolation or consent step for running targets, and runs unpinned npx packages.

not_examined: The skills CLI (skills.sh) and its install and update behaviour
REA itself and the benchmark targets (Notion.app, gh): no macOS and nothing was run
Raw outputs behind the context-overhead and tool microbenchmark tables (not committed)
Git history beyond one shallow commit
